March 28, 2025 Skyland Grain Explosion On March 28th at approximately 15:25 PM, the City of Sunray Gas Utility employees heard, felt and saw the explosion at the Skyland Grain elevator located at 110 E 2nd in Sunray Texas. Being familiar with the property and having knowledge of a City’s natural gas line in the area of the explosion, City employee attempted to close a gas valve on the South side of the elevator to isolate gas from flowing into the incident area. Unfortunately, operator was unable to isolate the gas line at that time. The operator was then given information of a gas line on fire on the North side of the elevator. With the operator being aware of the fact that Skyland Grain was supplied with gas from another gas company (TKO), he and another operator went to the location of the TKO gas meter. The operators were then able to see the gas line that was on fire and also see that the TKO gas meter was feeding gas to the elevator at a very high rate. The City operators then shut the valves off at the meter and could then see that the large gas line fire diminished as the gas flow was terminated. The City operators then located back to the South side to resume isolating the City gas line but were immediately told to evacuate the area as it was being “Red-Flagged” due to the extensive damage to the elevator. At this time, the City operators had to initiate another plan to isolate the flow of gas to the Skyland Grain property. The City operators then researched the gas maps again to determine how many valves and at what locations would need to be dug up and shut off in order to isolate the property. It was during this process of locating valves that the Fire Department determined that the City gas line had been damaged in the explosion as well and was currently flowing gas into the atmosphere, even though it was not on fire. It was at this time, approximately 22:05 PM, that the City of Sunray determined that due to the safety of many individuals and the magnitude of this situation, it was in the best interest for everyone to shut down the complete gas system. The City of Sunray gas system reached zero PSI at approximately 23:12 PM.

Subject: Pipeline strike on 9/22/25 Pipeline struck on 9/22/25 at 439 Eva James rd. Warsaw, NC. This is a summary of events from that day. At 11:02am, operator made aware of pipeline strike by local farmer. Farmer called and informed operator of the strike. Farmer asked what the appropriate steps were to take for this type of incident. Operator and farmer all agreed that safety was the immediate priority. Farmer instructed by operator to vacate the premise while operators closed isolation valved to struck pipeline length. Operator verifies valves were closed. Operator calls supervisor and environmental coordinator. Locks out closed valves. Operators onsite 11:45am. The farm owner met with operators and showed the strike location. Ops team took the following precautions for inspection; Established a barrier around the area, wore gas monitors, listened for any noise of rushing air from the area, ops took a sensitive methane sniffer as well. Ops approached the area making sweeps with the sniffer and eventually determined that methane was present in the trench only.. The trench the farmer had dug had methane present 10+ feet from the break. The trench was approximately 4-5 feet deep. We confirmed from the contractor that 811 was not called, we also confirmed there are no yellow gas markers within sight. Phone calls were made to farm staff. Ops maintained the barrier and after 15 minutes ops resampled the area noting that methane had dispersed the trench and was only present at the pipeline break. We determined it was safe enough to move the heavy equipment that was used to dig the trench to inspect further. No one entered the trench, ops sampled the trench with the sniffer prior to and during the evolution to ensure methane was not present. Afterwards, a discussion for repair was had. Those involved agreed that the repair was needed for safety at the forefront of any other dealings. The issue of who is responsible would be handled after the pipeline was repaired. The contractor who struck the pipeline offered to repair the pipeline and tracer wire at no charge since it was his crew that hit the pipeline and 811 was not called. After this discussion, we reiterated the importance of maintaining the barrier around the site. All those at the location were in agreement that work around the area would halt until after the repair was made and they would maintain the barrier. Ops maintained communication with all those involved and gave updates as needed. On 9/23/25 Repair to 4" HDPE line made using Electro-fusion couplings and the correct piping. Repaired the tracer wire. Addiitonalt sweeps made with the sniffer and area roped off, allowing only those who need to be in the area to be in the area. Ops dug a hole using an excavator to expose the pipe for repair. Air monitored in the hole continuously using an Altair 5X gas monitor. Ventilation blower was on hand if needed for proper air quality while personnel are in the hole. Repair made, and additional methan sweeps performed prior to opening the valves again. Area remonitored throughtout the day to check for lingering leaks. No further leaks after 8 hours. Trench refilled and marked.
